key_insight: In forced stably stratified turbulence, interface merging is driven by vertically sheared helical structures that break mirror symmetry, whereas their absence leads mainly to interface decay.
engineering_relevance: Understanding when stratified layers coarsen or persist helps predict mixing, density-interface stability, and transport in geophysical and industrial stratified flows.
method: Direct Numerical Simulations of forced stably stratified turbulence
Moderate-resolution runs with very long temporal integration to track slow coarsening
Correlation of interface motion with helicity dissipation and buoyancy flux
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that at low Fr = 0.076 kinetic-energy excursions coincide with vertical interface drift and merging, while at higher Fr = 0.22 the helical structures are absent and interfaces decay instead.
watch_item: The conclusions come from moderate-resolution DNS and may not fully generalize to higher Reynolds number or different forcing/stratification regimes.
paper_title: Drift of interfaces in forced stably-stratified turbulence and the role of vertically-sheared helical structures
